notes:
Row span. Cliopatria's Second Bulgarian Empire (1188..1394, 22 shapes) is one state. The dossier runs 1185 (infobox) to 1395 (Nikopol, 3 June; Cliopatria stops in 1394 and the infobox says 'Dissolved: Fall under Ottoman rule, 1422'); 1185-1187 and 1393-1395 are new keyframes. Vidin (1356) and Dobruja (1356) split off as the despotate-of-vidin and despotate-of-dobruja dossiers (other parts of eu-18); the Ottoman annexation of Vidin in 1396 and of Dobruja in 1411 are theirs.
Disagreements and silences. (1) Timing: the 1227 shape (228,826 km2) pre-dates Klokotnitsa (1230) and the infobox (293,000 km2 in 1230) matches the 1236 outline (312,296 km2, ratio 1.07), so the 1236 outline is used from 1230 (keyframes _1230, _1232; _1227 marked wrong). (2) Belgrade, Braničevo and Mačva: Cliopatria's Bulgarian shapes hold them in 1188-1201, 1206-1215 and 1236-1249 (checked with the gazetteer: Belgrade 16 of 19 cells, Braničevo 14 of 15, Mačva 13 of 14). The pages give Braničevo (and Belgrade, Stefan page) to Kaloyan in 1199, Hungary 'recaptured' in 1203, Boril cedes them in 1211, they return as a dowry in 1221 and Béla IV takes them in 1231/32 (Ivan Asen II page); Mačva is on no page. The keyframes follow the pages. The SBE article's undated 'occupying Belgrade and Braničevo' (in the 1246 section) and the Hungary dossier's 1255 may be the same event as 1231/32 or a retaking; no ledger event carries them. (3) Kaloyan: coronation 8 November 1204 (Kaloyan page) or 'late 1204' or 7 October 1205 (SBE page). (4) The page for Thessalonica names Michael II (SBE) while the Ivan Asen II page names Manuel.
